subject: Calculate standardized pooled estimates for SEM in runMI

messages.author: fd1e07b66a02a4fb
messages.subject: Calculate standardized pooled estimates for SEM in runMI
parts:
Hi all, 

First off, thank you for this group and the invaluable help provided. 

I would like to compute standardized estimates for the parameters in my SEM model based on 20 multiply imputed datasets. I have used runMI to fit the model below.

model1 <-

'#Measurement Model

 f1 =~ item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 + item5
 f2 =~ item6 + item7 + item8 + item9 + item10
 f3 =~ item11 + item12 + item13 + item14 + item15 +  item16 + item17
 f4 =~  item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 + item5 +  item6 + item7 + item8 + item9 + item10 +   item11 + item12 + item13 + item14 + item15 +  item16 + item17

 #Structural (partial mediation model)
Outcome2 ~ a*f4+ b*Outcome1 + f1 + f2 + f3 + gender + control2 + control3
Outcome1 ~ d*f4 +   f1 + f2 + f3 + gender + control2 + control3

#Derived effects
direct := a
indirect := d*b
total := (d*b) + a'

result <- sem.mi(model1, data = dat, orthogonal = TRUE, ordered = c("item1", "item2", "item3", "item4", "item5", "item6", "item7", "item8", "item9", "item10", "item11", "item12", "item13", "item14", "item15", "item16", "item17"))

Problem: When I estimate only the measurement model, the stand = TRUE argument works to get standardized estimates of the factor loadings. However, when I simultaneously estimate the measurement and structural model, I get this error: 

Error in lav_standardize_all(object, est = est, GLIST = GLIST, partable = partable,  :

  no slot of name "implied" for this object of class "lavaan.mi"

This thread explains that such an error occurs for models with exogenous predictors and ordinal outcomes. As per the solution provided, I have tried setting conditional.x = FALSE, however that seems to lead to problems of identification with negative variances and extremely high standard errors (~600) being estimated with all p values around 0.999. 

As per this thread, I have managed to calculate the pooled standardized estimates and standard errors. However, I understand that these are different from the standardized pooled estimates, as explained in the same thread, which I think is what I actually need (please correct me if wrong). 

My questions are:

1) Is there any way to use SemTools to output the standardized estimates for the regression coefficients for the above model?

2) If not, is there any way I can manually calculate them?  

I had posted part of this question as a reply to another thread, however I realized that was unclear and did not provide enough information hence posting as a new thread with more information and in a clearer manner. I apologize for the same. 

Thank you!

Warm regards,

Ritika

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Calculate standardized pooled estimates for SEM in runMI
parts: 2) If not, is there any way I can manually calculate them?

You can take the average of standardized coefficients across groups.  It will not be identical to the standardized pooled estimate, but it will be pretty close.  

I am working on a solution the lavaan.mi package, but it will take time that I currently don't have.

messages.subject: Re: Calculate standardized pooled estimates for SEM in runMI
parts:
You can install the new lavaan.mi package (along with the latest lavaan and semTools from GitHub) to access the new standardizedSolution.mi() function:
 
remotes::install_github("yrosseel/lavaan") 
remotes::install_github("TDJorgensen/lavaan.mi") 
remotes::install_github("simsem/semTools/semTools")

I deprecated runMI() functionality from semTools, and the lavaan.mi package is now updated with many bug-fixes and new features. Read the README and NEWS files closely before proceeding, because small changes have been made to the user interface (e.g., some argument names).

https://github.com/TDJorgensen/lavaan.mi

https://github.com/TDJorgensen/lavaan.mi/blob/main/NEWS.md

I hope to send this to CRAN by the end of the month or early July, and would appreciate the opportunity to debug these software updates before sending to CRAN.

I wonder if I could trouble you with one follow-up question. So I have been trying to see if I can calculate the standardized pooled estimates using: 

Standardized pooled estimate = mean of unstandardized estimates * SDx/SDy
Yes, that is essentially what is happening in the standardizedSolution.mi() function, using the pooled SD estimates.
I was wondering if you could point towards where I would find the model-implied SDs for x and y when they are observed variables for a lavaan.mi object? Would it be in fitted.values?

Yes.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Calculate standardized pooled estimates for SEM in runMI
parts: Is there a way I can a) still view the results of my previous fitted models and b) use the standardizedSolution function on my fitted models?

Not judging from what you shared.  In the new lavaan and lavaan.mi packages, there is now a @version slot to help monitor which software was used to fit a model.  Your case shows why this is important, so it can be tracked which bugs were undetected when a saved model was fitted.
